title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: after the order-theoretic preliminaries on bands and domination in a poset I (previous page), Grothendieck fixes the basic notion of an 'ordinary' stratification. This is the starting point for his programme of unfolding ('déploiement') stratified spaces into manifolds with boundary or corners via conical neighbourhoods.

Definition. Let X be a space and I an ordered set. An ordinary stratification of type I of X is a map I -> P(X), i |-> X_i, satisfying three conditions:
(Strat 1) each X_i is closed, and the family (X_i) is locally finite.
(Strat 2) i <= j implies X_i ⊂ X_j, so i |-> X_i is increasing.
(Strat 3) for all i, j, X_i ∩ X_j is the union of the X_k over the common lower bounds k of i and j (the set written [i∧j]).
The X_i are called the closed strata. 'Deux conditions' was later amended to three.

Modern reformulation. For x in X put I_x = {i : x ∈ X_i}. This set is:
- an up-set, by Strat 2;
- codirected (any two elements have a common lower bound in I_x), by Strat 3;
- finite, by local finiteness.
Hence, if nonempty, I_x has a least element s(x). The map s: X -> I satisfies s^{-1}(↓i) = X_i, which is closed. So s is continuous for the Alexandrov topology in which down-sets are closed.
On the next page Grothendieck sets X_i^* = X_i minus the union of the X_j with j < i. Then X_i^* = s^{-1}(i), and the next page's claim that the X_i^* partition X follows. So Strat 1-3, plus covering, amount to a locally finite poset-stratified space in the sense now used, for example in Lurie's Higher Algebra, Appendix A.

Resolution. For each flag d = (i_0 < ... < i_n) in I, set X_d = X_{i_0} (formula 88).
- Deleting a vertex of d gives an inclusion X_{i_0} ⊂ X_{min ∂d}.
- So d |-> X_d is a semi-simplicial space over X, functorial only for strictly increasing maps of standard simplices.
- Its realization is the Bousfield–Kan homotopy colimit over I of the diagram i |-> X_i.
- The fibre over x is the realization of the nerve of I_x, which is contractible because I_x has a minimum.
So this is a proper hypercovering-type 'semi-simplicial resolution' of X, as he says, and cohomological descent holds for closed locally finite covers.

Spectral sequence (89). For an abelian sheaf F on X there is a spectral sequence E_2^{p,q} = H^p(I, i |-> H^q(X_i,F)) => H^{p+q}(X,F).
- The coefficient system i |-> H^q(X_i,F) is contravariant in I, so H^p(I,-) means lim^p over I^op.
- This equals the semi-simplicial cohomology of Drap(I) with coefficients d |-> H^q(X_d,F), computed by the cochains ∏_{i_0<...<i_n} H^q(X_{i_0},F).
- It generalizes Godement's Mayer–Vietoris spectral sequence for locally finite closed covers, replacing the Čech nerve by the order complex of the poset.

Grothendieck then remarks that the closed strata are often complicated, so this dévissage is impractical. He announces passing to the open strata X_i^*, with X_d^* = X_{i_0}^*, which is done on the next page.
errors: The covering condition X = ∪ X_i is not stated among Strat 1-3, yet it is needed for the resolution claim and for the next page's 'partition de X'. It is presumably implicit; alternatively, points with I_x empty are simply not covered.
The text announces 'les deux conditions' but lists three. Strat 3 was evidently added afterwards; this is a slip, not a mathematical error.

The resolution claim is only qualified as 'en un sens convenable'. The justification (fibres are nerves of I_x, which have a least element, hence are contractible; plus proper base change for closed, locally finite covers) is not written. It is correct under Strat 1-3 together with covering.

Minor: H^p(I, -) must be read as cohomology of the poset with coefficients in a contravariant functor (lim^p over I^op), since i |-> H^q(X_i,F) is contravariant. The notation hides this, but the flag formula with X_{i_0} is consistent with it.

ideas.what: Ordinary stratification of type I: an increasing, locally finite family of closed subsets indexed by a poset, with X_i ∩ X_j = ∪_{k ≤ i,j} X_k. Equivalent to a continuous map X -> I (Alexandrov topology) with closed strata X_i = s^{-1}(↓i).
ideas.modern_name: Poset-stratified space (stratification over a poset with closed strata)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney/Thom/Mather for stratified spaces; the poset-valued formulation is usually cited from Lurie (Higher Algebra, Appendix A, ca. 2009–2017) and from earlier work on posets in stratified topology
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses tame stratified spaces informally, but not this poset axiomatics

ideas.what: Semi-simplicial space d |-> X_{min d} over the flags of I, resolving X
ideas.modern_name: Bousfield–Kan homotopy colimit / order-complex resolution of a closed poset cover (projection lemma)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bousfield–Kan (1972); Segal; later Ziegler–Živaljević (1993) and Welker–Ziegler–Živaljević (1999) for poset diagrams of spaces

ideas.what: Spectral sequence H^p(I, i |-> H^q(X_i,F)) => H^{p+q}(X,F) for a poset-indexed closed cover
ideas.modern_name: Mayer–Vietoris / descent spectral sequence for a closed cover indexed by a poset (lim^p over I^op)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Godement (closed-cover Mayer–Vietoris); cohomological descent (Deligne/Saint-Donat, SGA 4 Vbis); poset versions in combinatorial topology
ideas.where_published: Cohomological descent for proper hypercoverings is in SGA 4 Vbis (Saint-Donat), but not this poset form

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean but standard set-up: closed poset-indexed stratification, homotopy-colimit resolution over flags, and the resulting descent spectral sequence. The constructions are all known (Bousfield–Kan, Godement, cohomological descent, Lurie-style poset stratifications). The axiom Strat 3 neatly encodes continuity of X -> I, but this is not a new result.
transcription_corrections: Header: the crossed-out line is 'Une filtration de type I', with 'ordinaire' written above it. The new definition is 'stratification ordinaire'.

'et une reconnue [?]' is an uncertain reading of a marginal/interlinear addition after 'les deux conditions'. It apparently refers to the added third condition; the reading should remain flagged as doubtful.
The left-margin note reads roughly: 'les X_i s'appellent les "strates" fermées'.
'Les mêmes procédés pour tout faisceau' is more likely 'On a p.ex. pour tout faisceau abélien F sur X' (the 'p.ex.' is visible in the image).
'42' at the top left is Grothendieck's own manuscript pagination; '90' at the bottom is the archive page number.
